paragraphs.text: Massive limestone arches, tufas, and stalactites carved by the Río Mascún — steep, athletic terrain that rewards good tactics and solid head-games over raw strength alone. Exactly the kind of climbing this camp is designed to attack.

Patxi splits his coaching time between Rodellar and his home turf around Oliana and Coll de Nargo, so expect a few stories from further afield too — and route recommendations that go well beyond this single canyon.

overview: No harness. No rope. Just warm Mediterranean limestone above and impossibly turquoise water below, ready to catch you the moment your fingers inevitably let go.

Mallorca isn't just a good spot for deep water soloing — it's basically where the sport went mainstream, home to legendary lines climbed by names like Chris Sharma. You're not visiting a DWS destination. You're visiting the DWS destination.
Boat access gets you to secret crags most climbers never see, seven days of movement and mental-game coaching, and exactly zero crash pads standing between you and the sea.

hero.description: Six days of pure single-pitch sport climbing on the pale limestone of Cortina d'Ampezzo and Val Gardena — no ropes coiled for summits, no epics, just clean cragging and Italian sunshine.

overview: The Dolomites are famous for their towering multi-pitch objectives — but this trip isn't that. This is a week of pure single-pitch sport cragging on some of the same spectacular pale limestone, with none of the rope-management, route-finding, or all-day commitment that comes with big alpine routes.

Based in the charming towns of Cortina d'Ampezzo and Val Gardena, you'll work sun-warmed sport crags with quick approaches and quicker turnaround between routes — more burns, more mileage, more actual climbing time. Grades run from a friendly 5 all the way to 8c, so whether you're leading your first outdoor route or chasing a hard redpoint, there's a wall for you.
Six days of coaching from Klemen Bečan and Kostas Grafanaki, with a rest-day transfer between bases and properly legendary Italian food and wine to close out every evening.

paragraphs.text: A UNESCO World Heritage range of dramatic pale limestone peaks, home to hundreds of high-quality sport crags tucked beneath the famous towers and walls that make the Dolomites legendary — this trip sticks to the single-pitch sectors, leaving the big objectives for another day.

With an average of 21 days of sunshine a month through summer, conditions are about as reliable as alpine cragging gets, and the blend of Italian and Tyrolean food and culture makes every evening worth sticking around for.

overview: Finale Ligure is one of Europe's biggest sport climbing playgrounds — over 30 crags, 200+ sectors, thousands of routes of technical, pocketed limestone stacked in the hills above the Mediterranean. It's famous for rewarding movement over muscle, which makes it one of the best places on the continent to actually get better, not just tired.

This is our full two-week Sport Climbing Course: 12 days of coaching from refreshing your safety systems and leading technique through to redpoint and onsight tactics, delivered by Jan Novotny and Lucas Gangloff across the area's best single-pitch cragging.

Grades run from a friendly 5 up to 8c, so absolute beginners transitioning outdoors and climbers chasing hard numbers are equally at home — and every evening ends the same way, with good food, a swim if you want one, and more climbing talk than anyone needs.

hero.description: Six days deep in the birthplace of European free climbing — where metal protection is forbidden, knotted slings do the work, and the ethics haven't budged in over a century.

overview: Czech sandstone climbing is the birthplace of European free climbing, and it plays by its own rules entirely: no cams, no nuts, no metal touching the rock. Just knotted slings, textile rings, and a code of ethics that hasn't changed since routes here were first climbed in the early 1900s.

This is trad climbing as philosophy as much as technique. Wide Boyz climber Tom Randall has described the style as feeling almost like soloing, where the mind has to be every bit as strong as the hands. Expect delicate footwork on rock with the consistency of compressed sugar, minimal protection, and a level of mental fortitude that modern, well-bolted climbing rarely demands.
Six days building the skills, the ethics, and the head for it — capped with an attempt on a classic multi-pitch tower on your final day.

paragraphs.text: Slender spires and labyrinthine walls rising out of misty forests, like something out of a fantasy landscape. Many of these towers were first climbed in the early 1900s, some routes dating back to 1905 — and climbing them today, with the same techniques the pioneers used, is about as close to time travel as this sport gets.

The tradition has survived wars, political upheaval, and generations of climbers without bending its core rules. Even today, top climbers establishing new routes on Czech sandstone are expected to do it ground-up, out of respect for that history.

paragraphs.text: Rodellar is the steep, overhanging capital of Spanish sport climbing — massive limestone arches, tufas, and stalactites carved by the Río Mascún. It's physical, athletic climbing that rewards good tactics and solid head-games over raw strength alone.
That combination makes it the ultimate training ground for unlocking your first 7a, 7b, or 8a — exactly the terrain this camp is built around.

practicalCards.heading: Accommodation
practicalCards.body: Shared accommodation in local climbing hostels, cottages, campsites, campervans, or places run by local climbers. Want something more comfortable? We're happy to assist on request.

practicalCards.heading: Getting There
practicalCards.body: Fly into Barcelona. Local transport is organised via shared rental cars once you land — no navigating the Sierra de Guara solo.

practicalCards.heading: Gear
practicalCards.body: Bring your own climbing shoes and harness. We provide belay devices, helmets, and slings, but a screw-gate carabiner of your own is handy to have.

practicalCards.heading: Group Size
practicalCards.body: Minimum 3 participants to run the camp. Small enough for real coaching, focused entirely on your project.

faqs.question: What level do I need to be?
faqs.answer: A baseline redpoint grade of at least 6c to get the most out of this terrain. This camp is built for established sport climbers targeting their first 7a, 7b, or 8a — get in touch if you're unsure whether it's the right fit.

faqs.question: Do I need my own gear?
faqs.answer: Bring climbing shoes and a harness you trust. We provide belay devices, helmets, and slings, but a screw-gate carabiner of your own is worth packing. Full kit list sent once you book.

faqs.question: Is food included?
faqs.answer: Food is self-catering — supplies can be purchased any time during your stay, and there's a kitchen at the accommodation.

faqs.question: How does the work/climb balance actually work?
faqs.answer: Expect 10–12 climbing days across the two weeks, with the rest built in as recovery and remote-work time. Fast WiFi is provided, and the schedule is structured so your career and your project both get real attention.

faqs.question: What if fewer than 3 people book?
faqs.answer: We need a minimum of 3 participants to run the camp. If numbers don't add up, we'll offer an equivalent (or better) alternative trip, or a full refund. No hard feelings.

faqs.question: Where do I fly in and out of?
faqs.answer: Barcelona, for both arrival and departure.
